_about: Edge cases proposed with GenAI assistance (Claude) from docs/requirements.md and include/cell_noise.h, then executed and triaged. status 'pass' = must hold; 'known_limitation' = expected behaviour is NOT met today, tracked in docs/limitations.md, run as strict xfail so a fix is noticed.

cases.title: Very quiet cell, noise below one ADC LSB
cases.rationale: With 100 uV LSB, a real but very quiet cell can produce identical codes for a whole window. Does STUCK fire on a healthy cell?

cases.title: Inverter ripple coupled into the sense line
cases.rationale: Periodic interference has no single outlier but raises RMS; must be noise, not spike or drift.

cases.title: Interference synchronous to the sample rate (aliasing)
cases.rationale: If the disturbance frequency is a multiple of the sampling frequency, every sample sees the same phase.

cases.title: Slow voltage relaxation after a load step
cases.rationale: A slow exponential is almost linear over the window and should be reported as a trend.

cases.title: Fast voltage relaxation after a load step
cases.rationale: A fast exponential is strongly curved; a linear detrend leaves the curvature in the residuals.

cases.title: Single spike in the shortest allowed window (n = 8)
cases.rationale: In short windows one outlier has large leverage on the regression line and can inflate all other residuals.
cases.finding: DEF-001: was classified ELEVATED_NOISE; fixed by a robust refit without outliers

cases.title: Two adjacent spikes (EMI burst of two samples)
cases.rationale: Two consecutive outliers are still within spike_max_count and must not be treated as broadband noise.

cases.title: Spike on the first sample of a drifting window
cases.rationale: The first sample has the highest leverage; spike and drift must both be reported.

cases.title: Fully charged cell sitting exactly at v_max
cases.rationale: Noise makes about half the samples exceed v_max. The classifier has no hysteresis by design; debouncing belongs to the caller.

cases.title: Step change when cell balancing switches on mid-window
cases.rationale: Balancing current causes a sudden IR drop of a few mV. There is no STEP class; current behaviour is pinned here.

cases.title: Opposite spikes on both ends of a short window
cases.rationale: End points have maximum leverage; the fitted line can follow both outliers so neither looks like an outlier (masking).

cases.title: Intermittent open wire (every other sample reads 0 V)
cases.rationale: A loose connector can alternate between valid and zero readings; range check must win over noise.
